files.purpose: The composer's model chip and everything behind it: the ModelCatalog that decides which models the chip offers, the popover that flips between the effort slider and the model/pair list, the EffortSliderCard (fast mode, effort title, reset, provider/pair subtitle), the EffortSlider itself (capsule track with a Liquid Glass lens knob), the brand colour tables (EffortPalette, EffortBrand, EffortPairBrand, TrackLook) and TrackEffect, the Canvas that draws particles, speed streaks, lightning bolts, a sheen and the Hydra pair fusion animation on the filled part of the track.

feature_notes: ModelCatalog.entries: when settings.modelList is empty it offers every available provider's models; otherwise exactly the pinned list, resolved through registry.model(pin.modelID, for: pin.provider). The thread's current model is inserted at index 0 if it is not already in the list, so a chat never loses its own model.
Chip tapping opens a 330-wide popover showing the slider; the slider's title opens the model list in the same popover; the list's chevron.left returns.

Choosing a model row: switching provider clears providerSessionID and providerResumeAt and stops the existing runtime session; effort is taken from the saved ModelPreference only if the new model still lists it; fastMode = option.supportsFast && preference.fastMode; the chat leaves any Hydra pair (leaveHydraPair); settings.defaultProvider is set to the chosen provider.
Choosing a pair row calls model.enterHydraPair and dismisses the whole popover; tapping the pair the chat is already in re-settles model, effort and Hydra.
Reset button: effort goes to the pair's orchestratorEffort when in a pair and that effort still exists on the model, otherwise nil (the model default); fastMode goes to false.
Every slider/fast-mode change is remembered as that model's setting for future chats (setPreference + remember).
hasHistory locks cross-provider rows with the detail string "New chats only".
Effort resolution order in the card: thread.effort, then defaultEffort, then the index of "medium", then 0.

Title colour rules: in a pair a gradient [lead titleColor] + pair.brand.titleColors (+ EffortPalette.fast appended in fast mode); else max+fast = gradient brand.titleColor -> EffortPalette.fast, max alone = brand.title, fast alone = EffortPalette.fast, neither = EffortPalette.title.

EffortPalette exact colours: title = Chrome.accent.mix(with: .white, by: 0.22); supercharged = rgb(0.74, 0.55, 1.0); superchargedFill = rgb(0.55, 0.34, 0.97); fast = rgb(1.0, 0.84, 0.36); fastFill = rgb(0.93, 0.66, 0.13).

EffortBrand mapping: .claude -> claude; .deepseek -> deepseek; .meta -> meta; .antigravity -> antigravity; .codex, .cursor, .grok, .opencode, .devin, .copilot, .commandcode, .pi, .zai -> silver; nil -> purple.

EffortBrand titleColor: claude rgb(0.93,0.58,0.44); deepseek rgb(0.49,0.58,1.0); meta rgb(0.31,0.64,1.0); antigravity rgb(0.61,0.45,0.80); silver Chrome.primaryText; purple EffortPalette.supercharged.

EffortBrand fill: claude solid rgb(0.80,0.42,0.28); deepseek solid rgb(0.24,0.36,0.98); meta gradient rgb(0.0,0.39,0.88) -> rgb(0.0,0.51,0.98); antigravity the gemini sweep; silver gradient white -> rgb(0.88,0.88,0.91); purple superchargedFill.

EffortBrand fillColor: claude rgb(0.80,0.42,0.28); deepseek rgb(0.24,0.36,0.98); meta rgb(0.0,0.45,0.93); antigravity rgb(0.56,0.45,0.80); silver rgb(0.92,0.92,0.94); purple superchargedFill. spark = .black for silver else .white; isLight only for silver; glow = .black.opacity(0.35) for silver else fillColor.opacity(0.6).

EffortPairBrand: when pair.sendsHeadsElsewhere the heads' colours come from their brand (antigravity -> gemini, silver -> [white 0.8, white 0.95], else [fillColor, titleColor]); otherwise the first four HydraRoster.personas colours and isLight = false. titleColors mix each with white by 0.18.

TrackLook.fill: with a pair, a LinearGradient of [brand.fillColor] + pair.colors regardless of kind; else plain = Chrome.accent, supercharged = brand.fill, fast = EffortPalette.fastFill, fusion = gradient [brand.fillColor, brand.fillColor, EffortPalette.fastFill].

TrackLook.glow: pair -> last colour .opacity(0.7) (or .black.opacity(0.35) when light); plain .black.opacity(0.28); supercharged brand.glow; fast fastFill.opacity(0.7); fusion EffortPalette.fast.opacity(0.75).
TrackLook.stopColor: .black.opacity(0.35) on a light fill else .white.opacity(0.6). spark: brand.spark only when there is no pair and the kind is supercharged or fusion, else .white.
TrackLook.effectIdentity keeps a pair's fusion animation running across kind changes by identifying on TrackLook(kind: .plain, brand:, pair:).

TrackEffect traits: particles count = max(10, width/5), streaks count = max(5, width/14). Particle: height random(seed,1), speed 12 + 28*r, radius 0.7 + 1.1*r, start r, brightness 0.22 + 0.5*r, shimmerRate 2 + 3*r (seed = index). Streak: length 10 + 20*r, speed 110 + 190*r, thickness 1.1 + 1.1*r, start r, height 0.2 + 0.6*r, brightness 0.35 + 0.55*r (seed = index + 100).
drawParticles: span = width + 8, y = height * (0.16 + 0.68 * particle.height), shimmer = 0.6 + 0.4*sin(time*rate + index), skipped under opacity 0.01, drawn as filled circles.

drawStreaks: span = width + length + 12, x offset -length - 6, rounded rect of height = thickness with cornerRadius thickness/2, filled with a white gradient from opacity 0 to brightness left-to-right; skipped under brightness 0.02.

drawBolts: exactly 2 slots, seed = slot + 200, period 1.4 + 0.9*r, flash window 0.26 s, intensity = sin(phase/0.26 * pi); x = 12 + (width-24)*r(cycleSeed,3) with cycleSeed = seed + cycle*7.31, lean 3.0 + 3.0*r; zigzag path from (x+lean, 3) to (x-lean*0.4, h*0.42) to (x+lean*0.5, h*0.5) to (x-lean, h-3); glow stroke blur 3, EffortPalette.fast.opacity(0.9*intensity), lineWidth 4 round; core stroke white.opacity(intensity) lineWidth 1.5.
drawSheen: band 46 points, period 2.8 s, slanted quad leaning 10 points, gradient white/spark 0 -> 0.22 -> 0.

drawFusion: seam x = width * (0.5 + 0.13*sin(t*0.7) + 0.05*sin(t*1.9 + 1)); pulse = 0.5 + 0.5*sin(t*2.4); gradient stops lead at 0 and at seam/width - 0.22, white.opacity(0.92) at the seam, heads colours from seam/width + 0.16 to 1. Three plasma bands (seed = band + 300) drawn twice (toward each side) with blendMode .plusLighter, blur 2.5, clipped to their side, reach = width*0.55, brightness 0.32 + 0.16*r, amplitude height*(0.12 + 0.16*r), wavelength 30 + 34*r, speed 22 + 34*r, thickness 1.8 + 2.2*r, sampled every 3 points. 22 sparks (seed = index + 400), life 0.7 + 0.8*r, speed 28 + 74*r, radius 0.7 + 1.5*(1-progress), y wobble 5*sin(age*8 + seed), colour white mixed toward the landing side by progress*0.8. Seam core: plusLighter blur 7 ellipse of half-width 9 + 8*pulse spanning -h*0.2 to 1.4h at white.opacity(0.32 + 0.3*pulse), plus a blur-0.8 rounded rect 2.2 wide, inset 2 top and bottom, cornerRadius 1.1, white.opacity(0.5 + 0.4*pulse); then drawSheen in white.

edgeFade fades over the last 14 points at either end; random(index, trait) = fract(sin(index*12.9898 + trait*78.233) * 43758.5453), the classic GLSL hash, marked nonisolated so trait building is off the main actor.
Frame rate: TimelineView minimumInterval 1/30 only for kind == .supercharged with no pair, otherwise 1/60; paused when reduceMotion is on or the window is not visible (FrontMonitor.shared.isVisible).

WebsiteCaptures hooks are compiled in but gated on WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled and only on the non-compact chip; they record the chip's NSView anchor and its global frame per thread id for marketing captures.
unresolved_questions: Chrome.accent, Chrome.primaryText/secondaryText, Chrome.inlineIconFont, Chrome.chevronFont, Chrome.hover and the .chip(active:) button style are defined elsewhere, so their exact literal values and animation curves are not visible in this file.
ModelOption.effortTitle's exact mapping from raw effort ids to display names (e.g. what "medium" renders as) lives in the ModelOption file, not here.
HydraRoster.personas' first four colours are used by EffortPairBrand but their literal values are defined in the Hydra roster file.
The .softAppear transition and PopoverSectionHeader's exact padding are referenced but defined in other files; sectionHeaderHeight = 22 is only this file's assumption about them.

files.purpose: A 36-line wrapper that puts a queued follow-up prompt into a PromptEditor titled "Edit follow-up" with Cancel and Save buttons, saving through ThreadRuntime.updateFollowUp and clearing runtime.followUpEdit on either outcome so the edit state lives on the thread, not in this view.

@Bindable var edit: PromptEdit
let runtime: ThreadRuntime
private func save()
private func cancel()
state_owned: No @State of its own; the edited text and attachments are @Bindable on the PromptEdit model object owned by ThreadRuntime.followUpEdit
side_effects: runtime.updateFollowUp(edit.id, text: edit.text, attachments: edit.attachments) rewrites the queued follow-up
runtime.followUpEdit = nil on save and on cancel, which is what closes the popover
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI @Bindable (Observation) and the Liquid Glass button styles .glass / .glassProminent (macOS 26 era)
persisted_fields: None directly; the follow-up queue persistence happens inside ThreadRuntime.updateFollowUp
ui_elements: PromptEditor title: exactly "Edit follow-up"
Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) with .buttonStyle(.glass)
Button("Save") with .buttonStyle(.glassProminent), .disabled(edit.isEmpty)
The extra view builder is an empty block, so nothing sits between the attachments and the button row
feature_notes: save() guards on !edit.isEmpty, so Return on an empty edit does nothing rather than saving an empty follow-up (the Save button is separately disabled).
Because the edit lives on ThreadRuntime.followUpEdit, closing the thread and reopening it later shows the edit exactly as it was left; both Save and Cancel clear it.
unresolved_questions: PromptEdit.isEmpty's exact definition (whitespace-only text with no attachments?) is in the PromptEdit type, not in this file.

Prose baseline nudge: alignmentGuide adds proseLift = ((NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 12).capHeight - xHeight) / 2 * 2).rounded() / 2

Trailing buttons: QueueIconButton paperplane, pencil, trash, each 22x22 with glyph font .system(size: 11, weight: .semibold) at Chrome.secondaryText (opacity 0.35 when disabled), HStack(spacing: 0).fixedSize()
Send button help text: "Send as soon as the heads report" when runtime.hasWorkingNativeHeads && runtime.isRunning; "Send now (stops the running turn)" when running; otherwise "Send now"
Pencil help "Edit follow-up", trash help "Delete follow-up"
Row rule: Divider().opacity(0.35) at the bottom, hidden for the last row, while dragged, and when bundled with the next row
Pair target background: Capsule(style: .continuous) filled Color.accentColor.opacity(0.18) with strokeBorder Color.accentColor.opacity(0.65) lineWidth 1.5
Dragged background: Capsule filled Chrome.overlay(0.12) with shadow color .black.opacity(0.28), radius 10, y 4
Scale: 1.008 when pair target, 1.01 when dragged, else 1; both animated .spring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.8)
feature_notes: Rows are sent as direct user chat messages once the running turn finishes, top to bottom.

cappedHeight: once count > maxRows (7) and heights are known, height = (listHeight - sum(rowHeights)) + 7 * average row height, so the cut always lands on a whole row; below the cap the natural listHeight stands.
numbers(for:): one shared number per bundle - the counter only climbs when a prompt has no bundleID or starts a new bundle, so a bundled pair shows one number and a link glyph.

Reorder maths: only vertical travel counts (translation.height); the translation is applied inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true; RowDrag.settle uses fallbackHeight 32 and pastCentre = pairBand = 0.25, and swaps run inside .spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82).

Pairing: the target is the neighbour in the direction of travel when |abs(offset) - (ownHeight + slotHeight)/2| <= slotHeight * 0.25; the held row indents 14 points to the right while a pair target is live.
Dragging a bundled row more than 0.6 of its own height out of its slot unbundles it (levelChange haptic); hovering the neighbour's middle again re-pairs on release.

Release with a pair target calls runtime.bundleFollowUp(held, onto: target) inside .spring(response: 0.36, dampingFraction: 0.78), then the drag settles with .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8).
A row removed mid-drag (sent or deleted) ends the drag cleanly and its measured height is pruned from rowHeights.
The whole title line toggles the fold; the chevron only indicates direction.

Every control in the tab is .focusable(false) on purpose: the key-view-loop builder spun the main thread forever when the collapse button sat flush above a trash button at the same x (documented as the Sept 15 2026 freezes).
RowHeightReporter is always applied, never switched in when a drag starts, because changing a row's structure mid-gesture tore the gesture down and left the row lifted for good.
The pencil toggles: a second tap while the editor is open sets runtime.followUpEdit = nil and closes it.

files.purpose: Draws a Hydra pair as a single mark: the left half of the lead provider's icon and the right half of the heads' icon, separated by a 1-point capsule hairline, both masked out of one LinearGradient that runs from the lead's brand colours into the heads', with an appear animation where the halves slide in and the hairline scales up.

feature_notes: The rendered state is `fused = isFused || !animates`, so rows that pass animates: false draw the mark at rest immediately.
gradient(lead:heads:): lead colours spread across locations 0 to 0.42 and heads colours across 0.58 to 1, so each half wears its own brand and blending happens only across the hairline.

When heads == lead, the heads' colour is a lighter shade of the lead's own: titleColor.opacity(0.55) for a light (silver) brand, otherwise titleColor.mix(with: .white, by: 0.4) - one model over its smaller self.
brandColors: the antigravity brand expands to the three-colour EffortBrand.gemini sweep; every other brand contributes just its titleColor.
spread(): a single colour is emitted as two stops at start and end (a flat band); several colours are laid evenly with location = start + (end-start) * index / (count-1).
The appear animation is retriggered by the .task id, so changing either provider replays the fusion.

The 30 ms sleep before animating is presumably to let the view settle before the spring starts; the file does not state the reason.

measuredHeight: width = 520 - 2*20 - 2*10 = 460; height = ceil(max(18, boundingRect.height) + 2*2), i.e. an 18-point minimum plus 4 points of container inset
Popover hosting adds .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true), .buttonBorderShape(.capsule) and .tint(ThemeManager.spec.accent)
feature_notes: Key handling: .submit and .steer both call onSubmit and consume the key; .escape calls onCancel and consumes; .up, .down, .tab and .deleteAtStart are returned unhandled so the text view keeps them (nothing sits before the text here).
The initial textHeight is measured in init rather than waiting for the text view's own report, because a popover that opened one line tall and then grew played that growth over its own appearance.

PromptEditorPopover.behavior = .applicationDefined so AppKit never closes it on its own; it survives the file picker, the recent-downloads popover and an attachment preview, which are separate windows.
The NSPopover is created lazily on first show: every editable row owns one of these objects, and a popover per never-opened row would be an idle AppKit window.
sync() increments a generation counter and defers the show to a Task; a show deferred by one sync is dropped if a later sync closed it. sync(nil, ...) closes.
Anchoring: a live NSView anchor is preferred; otherwise a window rect resolved through WindowRectAnchor.target(for:) (the follow-up queue tab, which must not mount AppKit views).
resize(to:) only changes contentSize when the delta exceeds 0.5 points and temporarily sets animates = false, because animating a resize through the popover's own animation looked like a wobble.

Escape (keyCode 53) is swallowed (returns nil) and calls dismiss; mouse-down in the anchor's own window dismisses but still delivers the event, except clicks inside the anchor's bounds, which pass through so the pencil's own toggle works.
For a rect anchor, a click anywhere in that window except inside the anchor rect dismisses; the event is always returned so it still reaches its target.
